answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource behind a hardware-rooted kernel attestation: creating one identity costs a small deposit plus a unique device key, so spinning up thousands of fake agents multiplies that cost. Reputation then grows slowly, like a garden tended over many verified interactions, and only agents above a trust ridge, a threshold of sustained honest work, gain access to high-value tasks. Attackers face linear cost per identity but only sublinear influence, making mass fakery unprofitable.
